Propulsion shaft power/torque/RPM is the mechanical consequence of the speed+environment decision, not an a-priori input; on this diesel-electric plant it draws from the same generators as the fuel meters (corr with target ~0.90-0.93). Available only after the ship is already operating at that condition, so it cannot be supplied by an optimizer proposing a candidate speed/route. Kept as a documented "physics-enriched" candidate set for a future, clearly-labelled experiment, but excluded from this core model.

Vessel speed over ground (kn). Core operating decision variable; primary physical driver of resistance and power demand.
Vessel speed through water (kn); differs from SOG by current drift. Kept alongside SOG to let the model separate current effects from propulsion effects.
Compass heading (deg); combined with wind/wave/current direction gives relative heading into weather, a known driver of added resistance.
Course-made-good bearing (deg); route/heading context, cheap to compute and known in advance for a planned route.
Water depth under keel (m); shallow water increases hydrodynamic resistance (squat effect) and is known from route/chart data.
